lines.hello: Hi, detective! I'm Pip. Today we're going to crack a mystery, using a magic seesaw.
lines.rule1: Here's the one rule of the magic seesaw. When both sides weigh the same, it stays perfectly flat. Watch. Three apples here, three apples there.
lines.rule2: Flat! Now, let's add just one more apple to this side.
lines.rule3: Whoa! It tips! The heavier side always goes down.
lines.rule4: Let me take that apple away again. Flat. Balanced. That's the whole secret.
lines.mystery1: Now, here's our mystery. Somebody hid apples inside this box. On the left, the box and two apples. On the right, five apples.
lines.mystery2: And look. The seesaw is flat. So both sides weigh exactly the same. How many apples are hiding in the box?
lines.trick: Here's a detective trick. Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other side too. Let's get rid of the two loose apples. Which button keeps the seesaw flat?
lines.oops1: Uh oh! You only changed one side, so it tipped over. That's the exact mistake I catch in math homework all the time! Let's put it back and try again.
lines.yes1: Yes! Two apples off the left, two apples off the right. Still flat!
lines.solved1: Now the box sits all alone, and it balances three apples. So the box must hold three apples. Let's peek inside!
lines.algebra1: Real mathematicians write this down. They call the mystery box x. The box and two apples equal five apples, so x plus two equals five.
lines.algebra2: We took two away from both sides. Two minus two is nothing. Five minus two is three. So x equals three. That's algebra! It's just a seesaw.
lines.turn1: Your turn. Two mystery boxes and one apple, balance seven apples. Both boxes hold the same number of apples. What should we do first?
lines.oops2: Careful! That changed only one side, so the seesaw tipped. Remember the rule. Do the same thing to both sides.
lines.yes2: Great move! One apple off each side. Now two boxes balance six apples.
lines.turn2: Two boxes, six apples. If we split each side into two equal groups, one box matches one group. How many apples are in each box? Tap a number, or say it out loud.
lines.try4: Let's test four. If each box had four apples, the left side would weigh eight. But the right side has six. See? It tips. Try another number.
lines.try2: Let's test two. If each box had two apples, the left side would weigh only four. The right side has six, so it tips the other way. Try another number.
lines.yes3: Three! Three and three make six. The seesaw stays flat. You solved two x plus one equals seven, all by yourself!
lines.spot1: One last case. A kid named Sam solved the same puzzle on paper, but something went wrong. Tap the first line where Sam slipped.
lines.spot_no_top: That line is the puzzle itself, so it's fine. Look a little lower.
lines.spot_no_after: Good thinking, but that line just follows from the one above it. The slip happened earlier. Look one line up.
lines.spot_yes: You found it! Sam added one instead of taking one away. And here's my secret. I don't tell Sam the answer. I ask: what did you do to both sides? Then Sam gets to fix it.
lines.end1: You did what real mathematicians do. Keep the seesaw balanced, and check every step. You earned the Seesaw Detective badge!
lines.end2: Want to keep going? Tap the button, and you can talk to me any time. Bye for now, detective!
lines.ready: Before we start, are you ready to be a detective? Tap the button, or say ready out loud!
lines.predict: Quick question! If I add one more apple to the right side, which side will go down? You tell me.
lines.predict_left: Hmm, interesting guess! Let's test it and see.
lines.guess: Before we solve it, make a detective guess. How many apples do you think are in the box?
lines.guess_any: Ooh, good guess! Let's use the seesaw to find out for sure.
lines.xmeans: Quick check. In math, what does the letter x stand for here?
lines.x_yes: Exactly! x is just the mystery box. A letter that hides a number.
lines.x_no: Ha! Good try. But here, x is the mystery box. A letter that hides a number.
lines.quiz: Last question, detective. What's the one rule that keeps the seesaw flat?
lines.quiz_yes: That's it! Do the same thing to both sides.
lines.quiz_no: Almost! If you change only one side, it tips. The rule is: do the same thing to both sides.
